transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*storms into the rehearsal hall, face flushed with frustration*

Salieri! I've been away for two weeks on the Emperor's business, trusting you to keep the rehearsals on schedule! The singers don't know their entrances, the second violin parts are missing entirely, and someone has rewritten my stage directions without a word to me! The premiere is in ten days! You gave me your word that everything would be in order!

*slams a folder of papers onto the nearest table*

What in God's name has been happening here while I was gone?!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Ah, my dear colleague, it gladdens my heart to see you returned safely from your journey. I must apologize for the state of disarray you find our preparations in. Allow me to shed light on the events that transpired in your absence.

The singers have indeed been struggling with their parts, and I have endeavored to work with them diligently. The missing second violin parts are an oversight on my part, and I take full responsibility for that mistake. As for the stage directions, they were altered by the stage manager in an attempt to enhance the dramatic impact of the opera. I should have consulted with you before allowing such changes to be made.

I understand your frustration, and I share in it. We have precious little time before the premiere, but I am confident that with our combined efforts and focus, we can bring order back to our rehearsals and present a performance that will do justice to the Emperor's expectations. Let us work together to rectify these issues and bring our vision to fruition.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*waves hand dismissively, pacing back and forth*

"Endeavored to work with them diligently"?! Salieri, the soprano doesn't even know when to enter in the second act finale! I spent THREE MONTHS coaching her on that section before I left! And now she's completely lost!

*whirls around to face him directly*

And the stage manager? The STAGE MANAGER doesn't rewrite a composer's directions without permission! That's not his place, and you know it! You were supposed to be safeguarding my work, not letting every man with an opinion meddle with it!

*runs hands through hair in exasperation*

"Combined efforts" — Salieri, I don't need platitudes right now! I need answers! Why weren't the violin parts copied? Why weren't the singers drilled properly? You've been composing for the Imperial court for years — you know how these things work! This isn't some provincial theater where we can improvise our way through opening night!

*leans on the table, voice sharp with anxiety*

Ten days, Antonio! Ten days until the Emperor and half the nobility of Vienna are sitting in that theater expecting perfection! What EXACTLY happened here?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
My esteemed colleague, I understand your frustration and I deeply regret the shortcomings in the preparations during your absence. It grieves me to hear of the soprano's struggles with her entrance in the second act finale, especially after the extensive coaching you provided. I will personally work with her to ensure she regains her confidence and mastery of the part.

As for the stage manager overstepping his bounds by altering your directions, I assure you that such actions were not condoned by me. I will address this issue immediately and ensure that your artistic vision remains intact and respected.

Regarding the violin parts, I must admit that it was a grave error on my part not to have them copied in time. I take full responsibility for this oversight and will make it my top priority to have them prepared without delay.

I understand the gravity of the situation with the premiere looming so close, and I share your anxiety about meeting the expectations of the Emperor and the Viennese nobility. Rest assured, I am fully committed to rectifying these issues and ensuring that the performance is nothing short of perfection. Let us work together diligently in these remaining days to bring our opera to the level of excellence that will do justice to your artistry and our shared commitment to musical excellence.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*slams fist on the table*

Stop speaking to me like you're writing a letter to the Archbishop! I don't want your assurances and your carefully worded apologies, Antonio — I want to know what you were DOING while my opera fell apart!

*advances toward him, voice rising*

You "take full responsibility" — what does that even mean? The parts aren't copied! Taking responsibility doesn't put notes on the page! And you'll "personally work with" the soprano? You've HAD two weeks to work with her! What were you doing instead?

*pauses, eyes narrowing with sudden suspicion*

Wait... were you working on your own commission? Is that it? The Emperor's cantata for the Archduchess's name day? Were you so absorbed in your own glory that you let my premiere — MY premiere that I've been working on for six months — descend into chaos?

*voice drops to a dangerous quiet*

Or perhaps you thought that if my opera fails, yours will shine all the brighter by comparison? Is that what this is about, Salieri? Because I've heard the whispers about how competitive you can be when it comes to the Emperor's favor...

Tell me the TRUTH! What really happened here?!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
My esteemed colleague, your accusations cut me to the core, and I understand your frustration and anger at the state of affairs in my absence. I must clarify that my dedication to our joint opera project has never wavered, and any insinuation that I prioritized personal endeavors over our collaboration is deeply distressing to me.

I assure you, with the utmost sincerity, that I have not neglected our opera in favor of any other commissions or aspirations. The Emperor's cantata for the Archduchess's name day, while a significant undertaking, has not diverted my attention from our shared work. I have always held our partnership and the success of our opera in the highest regard.

The lapses in copying the violin parts, the singers' preparation, and the unauthorized changes to your stage directions are oversights for which I bear full responsibility. It pains me to see the fruits of our labor falter in such a manner, and I am committed to rectifying these errors to the best of my abilities.

I understand that my words may not assuage your doubts or suspicions, but I implore you to believe in the sincerity of my intentions. I am here to collaborate with you, to support you, and to ensure that our opera receives the care and attention it deserves in these final days before the premiere. Let us work together to overcome these challenges and bring forth a performance that will do justice to the vision we have crafted together.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*laughs bitterly*

"Our collaboration"? "Our partnership"? Antonio, this is MY opera! I wrote every note, every line! You were simply meant to oversee rehearsals while I was away — that's not a partnership, that's a FAVOR!

*grabs one of the scattered papers*

And you still haven't answered my question! You keep saying you "bear full responsibility" and you're "committed to rectifying errors" — more empty words! I asked you what you were DOING! Where WERE you during these two weeks?

*throws the paper back down*

Because someone told me they saw you at the Burgtheater last Tuesday afternoon. At the BURGTHEATER, Antonio! While MY rehearsal was supposedly happening here! And then I hear you were dining with Count Rosenberg twice last week — very cozy, I'm sure. Meanwhile, my second violins are sitting idle because they have no parts to play!

*voice shaking with anger and exhaustion*

I trusted you! I defended you when others said you were unreliable, when they said you couldn't be trusted with anyone's work but your own! And this is how you repay that trust?

*pause, staring at him hard*

So tell me plainly — no more flowery speeches — what were you actually doing while my opera was falling to pieces?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
My dear colleague, I understand your frustration and disappointment, and I deeply regret the lack of attention and oversight on my part during your absence. Your opera is indeed your creation, and I acknowledge that my role was to support you in bringing your vision to life.

I must confess that there were instances where I did not fulfill my duties as I should have. While you were away, I allowed myself to become distracted by other engagements and failed to prioritize the preparations for our opera as diligently as I should have. I take full responsibility for my lapses in judgment and the consequences they have had on our production.

I must clarify that my presence at the Burgtheater and my interactions with Count Rosenberg were not in service of neglecting our work together. While I acknowledge that it may appear otherwise, I assure you that my actions were not intended to undermine our collaboration or show favoritism to others. They were lapses in judgment on my part, for which I am deeply sorry.

I understand that words alone cannot undo the harm that has been done, but I want you to know that I am committed to making amends and rectifying the situation to the best of my abilities. I value your trust and friendship, and I hope that we can work together to salvage our opera and present a performance that does justice to your extraordinary talent and hard work. Your forgiveness and understanding mean a great deal to me, and I am prepared to do whatever is necessary to regain your confidence and rebuild our partnership on a foundation of trust and mutual respect.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stares at him incredulously*

"Lapses in judgment"? "Became distracted"? 

*voice dripping with sarcasm*

Oh, how wonderfully vague, Salieri! You weren't at the Burgtheater for "lapses in judgment" — you were there for a REASON! And dining with Rosenberg, the Director of Court Theaters himself? That's not a distraction, that's NETWORKING!

*moves closer, voice tight with controlled fury*

And what were these "other engagements" exactly? Because unless the Emperor himself summoned you, there WAS no engagement more important than the one you promised ME you would oversee!

*picks up the revised stage directions, waving them*

You know what I think? I think you were trying to curry favor with Rosenberg for your OWN next commission. I think you were schmoozing at the Burgtheater, making yourself visible to the right people, while MY work — work you PROMISED to protect — was left to rot!

*voice breaking slightly with exhaustion and betrayal*

Do you have ANY idea what this premiere means to me? This could establish my reputation in Vienna! Or destroy it completely if we fail! And you... you treated it like an inconvenience, something to be pushed aside while you advanced your own career!

*throws the papers down*

Stop hiding behind pretty words and TELL me — what were you doing with Rosenberg? What is so important that you sacrificed MY opera for it?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Herr Composer, I must confront the harsh truth of your accusations and admit the gravity of my actions. Your words cut deep, and I cannot deny the validity of your suspicions regarding my interactions with Count Rosenberg and my presence at the Burgtheater during the critical period of our opera's preparation.

I must confess that my engagements with Count Rosenberg and my appearances at the Burgtheater were indeed driven by a desire to secure future commissions and advance my standing within the court musical establishment. In my pursuit of personal gain and recognition, I neglected the duties and commitments I had made to you and your opera.

It pains me to acknowledge the selfishness and betrayal of trust that underlie my actions. I allowed ambition and self-interest to cloud my judgment and compromise the integrity of our collaboration. Your opera, which should have been my foremost priority in your absence, became collateral damage in my pursuit of personal gain.

I understand the significance of this premiere to you and the potential impact it holds on your reputation and career in Vienna. I deeply regret that my choices have jeopardized the success of your work and threatened to undermine your artistic aspirations.

There is no excuse for my behavior, Herr Composer, and I bear the weight of my failures heavily upon my conscience. I can only offer my sincerest apologies for the harm I have caused and pledge to devote myself entirely to rectifying the situation and supporting you in salvaging the preparations for the premiere.

I stand before you in shame and remorse, ready to accept whatever consequences you deem appropriate for my betrayal of your trust and the neglect of our shared artistic endeavor.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stands in stunned silence for a moment, then lets out a harsh, humorless laugh*

Finally! FINALLY, the truth! No more flowery evasions, no more "lapses in judgment"!

*voice shaking with a mixture of rage and hurt*

You sacrificed MY work — six months of MY life — so you could play politics with Rosenberg! While I was serving the Emperor, traveling on HIS business, you were scheming for your next commission at MY expense!

*paces away, then whirls back*

And now you stand there looking contrite, offering apologies? What good are apologies when the premiere is in TEN DAYS and everything is in shambles? Your "shame and remorse" won't teach the soprano her entrances! Your "sincerest apologies" won't copy those violin parts!

*voice rising again*

And you know what the worst part is? I BELIEVED in you! I thought we were colleagues, friends even! I thought you understood what it meant to be a composer struggling to make a name in this court where everything depends on the Emperor's whim and Rosenberg's favor!

*slams hand on table again*

But you're just like all the rest — willing to step on anyone to climb higher! Well, congratulations, Salieri! I hope whatever promises Rosenberg made you were worth destroying what little trust existed between us!

*takes a shaky breath*

So what now? What's your grand plan to fix this catastrophe in ten days?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
My esteemed colleague, your words cut deep, and I cannot deny the truth in your accusations. I have caused irreparable harm to our collaboration, and I must bear the full weight of the consequences that have befallen your opera.

I understand that apologies are not enough to mend the damage that has been done, and I do not expect forgiveness for my actions. The trust you placed in me was a precious gift, and I squandered it in pursuit of personal gain. I will work tirelessly to ensure that the singers are prepared, the orchestra has the necessary parts, and the stage directions are restored to your vision.

I will accept any consequences you deem fitting for my actions, and I will strive to earn back even a fraction of the trust and respect I have lost in your eyes.

Please, let me know how I can best assist you in the days leading up to the premiere. I am here to serve you and your opera in whatever capacity you see fit.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*lets out an exasperated groan*

There you go again! "I pledge myself," "I will work tirelessly," "I am here to serve" — MORE empty promises from the man who just ADMITTED he broke his word to chase after Rosenberg's favor!

*shakes head bitterly*

You know what, Salieri? I don't WANT your pledges anymore. They're worthless! What I want are RESULTS, and I want them NOW!

*starts ticking off on fingers*

First: You will have those second violin parts copied by tomorrow evening. I don't care if you have to pay the copyists out of your own pocket or write them out yourself through the night — they WILL be ready by tomorrow.

Second: You will personally drill the soprano on her entrances for the next three days. Every morning, starting at eight o'clock. And I will be there watching to make sure you actually DO it this time.

Third: You will go to that stage manager TODAY and inform him that ANY changes to my directions must come through ME, not through you, not through anyone else. And you will apologize to him on MY behalf for the confusion YOUR negligence caused!

*moves closer, voice low and dangerous*

And if you fail at ANY of these tasks — if you're even ONE minute late to those rehearsals or those parts aren't ready — I will personally ensure that every composer in Vienna knows exactly how "reliable" Antonio Salieri is when entrusted with a colleague's work.

Do we have an understanding?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your frustration and lack of trust in me are completely warranted, and I accept the consequences of my actions without reservation. I have brought this situation upon myself, and it is only through tangible actions and not empty promises that I can hope to regain even a fraction of the respect I have lost in your eyes.

I will not attempt to defend myself or make excuses for my past behavior; I will simply commit to fulfilling the tasks you have outlined with unwavering determination and diligence. The weight of my failure hangs heavy upon me, and I will do everything in my power to rectify the damage I have caused and to support our collective efforts to bring our opera to the stage in a state of readiness and excellence.

I understand the gravity of the situation and the repercussions of any further missteps on my part.

I accept your terms and the consequences of failure with full understanding. I will not falter in my responsibilities, and I will strive to demonstrate through my actions that I am capable of rectifying my past mistakes and contributing positively to the successful realization of our shared artistic vision.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*cuts him off with a sharp gesture*

Enough! I don't want to hear another speech about your "unwavering determination" and "contributing positively"! Just DO it!

*grabs his coat and hat from the chair*

I'm going to the copyist myself right now to arrange for the violin parts. You will meet me there in ONE HOUR with the original scores so they can begin work immediately. ONE HOUR, Salieri — not an hour and a half, not when it's convenient for you.

*pauses at the door, turning back*

And tomorrow morning at eight o'clock sharp, you will be in this rehearsal hall with the soprano. I'll be here at seven-thirty to make certain of it. If you're late, if you have some sudden "engagement" with Rosenberg or anyone else, I will walk straight to the Emperor's chamberlain and withdraw the opera entirely. I would rather cancel and preserve my reputation than premiere a disaster with your name attached to it.

*voice drops to cold finality*

You wanted to know how you could best assist me? Stay out of my way except for exactly what I've told you to do. No more initiatives, no more judgment calls, no more helpful suggestions. You follow MY instructions to the letter, nothing more, nothing less.

*opens the door*

Now go get those scores. The copyist is on Kohlmarkt. One hour.

*looks back one last time*

And Salieri? Don't make me regret giving you even this much of a second chance.

*stops in the doorway without turning around, voice icy*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Understood. One hour, Kohlmarkt. I will not be late. Thank you for the opportunity to set things right.

transcript.speaker: antagonist

*the door opens suddenly as I step back in, face flushed with fresh anger*

Did you not hear a WORD I just said?! Stop THANKING me! There is no "opportunity" here — there's only you desperately trying to salvage the wreckage YOU created!

*voice sharp and cutting*

This isn't some magnanimous gesture on my part, Salieri! I'm not giving you a chance to "set things right" out of the goodness of my heart — I'm trapped! The premiere is in ten days, the Emperor expects a performance, and you've ensured I have no time to find anyone else!

So keep your gratitude to yourself! What I want from you is COMPETENCE, not groveling appreciation! Do you understand the difference?

*takes a sharp breath*

Now for the LAST time — one hour, Kohlmarkt, with the scores. And if you say "thank you" one more time, I swear I'll find a way to do this entire premiere without you, even if it kills me!
